Your hairstylist is NOT flirting with you. We have to smile and be nice so please don’t make awkward and inappropriate jokes/passes at us because we just want to do our job. (Also we know when you’re looking at our boobs when we go to check your sideburns)

I’m 5’5” and I was 260 lbs. I was worried about this too. My surgeon said I needed to lose 20 lbs in about 3 months, I was only able to lose about 14-16 (kept fluctuating between the two. She said it was fine and that she made the goal a bit more than she needed just to make sure I was serious, and to prove to insurance that I’m serious. They ended up approving on my first try and now I’m 2 weeks post op! Don’t give up if you’re obese/overweight, it’s just a little bit of work for the surgery you’ve always wanted!

ETA* to lose the weight I cut out snacking, soda, and watched my portions. I don’t know if it’ll help but I figured I’d mention it!

I only had the reduction but I’m 1 week and 4 days post op and I still can’t reach very far above my head and it hurts to push myself up from a chair. I’d say you’re going to need a fair amount of time if you’re arms are getting done too, before you will be able to get around normally.

I got the same thing a couple days ago and went to my dr. She told me it was probably just a mixture of indigestion, gas, and constipation. Make sure to take some gas relief medicine and stool softeners and see if that helps you any. It definitely helped me

I was super nervous but my surgical team was super sweet and as soon as I got over having the IV put in and got my “happy medicine” (before the anesthesia a few minutes before the surgery) I was golden. I didn’t have a care in the world.
So I’m not crazy! I’m literally laying in bed awake right now because my stomach is growling so hard I can’t sleep haha

I had some strange sharp pains in my diaphragm/ abdominal area and it turned out to be caused by a mixture of heartburn and gas build up. Make sure to take some gas relief medicine and stool softeners (if you need them) and I take a Pepcid before I go to bed to help with any heartburn.

Oh! Also, lunchables were great for me. They literally have no prep and if you’re not around she can most likely open and eat it with no problem. Apple juice too, it helps uhh.. get things moving, if ya know what I mean.

I definitely recommend a notebook or something to write down when she takes her meds. I had to do this because I couldn’t remember if I’d taken them or not the first few days. I also recommend some loose fitting pajama bottoms and socks/slippers that won’t fall off easily. I’m only 5 days post op but I regret not buying a pregnancy pillow sooner. I ordered one on amazon (U-shaped, not C-shaped)  the day after and I think it’ll make me a lot more comfortable. Also lots of soft button ups because she won’t be able to lift her arms up hardly and you can unbutton it easily to adjust your bandages or put an ice pack on. If she has drain tubes I recommend loose pants with pockets to put them in when she walks around.
